channel.title: New research | AI & Attention Observatory
channel.description: New studies and ideas about AI, cognition, and attention. Research notes link to the original evidence.

item.title: A single kill switch cannot stand in for continuous oversight of distributed AI systems and human decisions.
item.description: Perspective: A single kill switch cannot stand in for continuous oversight of distributed AI systems and human decisions. The idea of a single emergency switch makes AI governance look like a matter of one decisive act. Wintermeier argues that this image hides the distributed infrastructure of advanced systems and the human decisions that shape their behavior before any emergency occurs.

item.title: Emotionally responsive AI improved some learning experiences, not measured learning gains over ChatGPT.
item.description: Research finding: Emotionally responsive AI improved some learning experiences, not measured learning gains over ChatGPT. In a randomized high-school trial, adding self-regulation prompts and emotional support changed how students felt and engaged during the task, but did not establish superior knowledge or transfer gains.

item.title: What makes sustained attention easier or harder?
item.description: Research question: What makes sustained attention easier or harder? This study aimed to investigate the relationship between response time variability and levels of ADHD symptoms both in this new, low-arousal sustained attention task and in the Sustained Attention to Response Task (SART).

item.title: How do people monitor and regulate their thinking with technology?
item.description: Research question: How do people monitor and regulate their thinking with technology? This theory-building systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence on metacognition, trust, and human–AI co-regulation in GenAI-supported foreign language learning.

item.title: How do people monitor and regulate their thinking with technology?
item.description: Research question: How do people monitor and regulate their thinking with technology? This study contributes a scalable, human-centred and ethically grounded model for improving both learning outcomes and learner experience in digital education environments.

item.title: Fast-moving children’s media can hold the gaze while leaving too little room to think through what is happening.
item.description: Perspective: Fast-moving children’s media can hold the gaze while leaving too little room to think through what is happening. Media quality cannot be reduced to screen-time totals or educational subject matter. Kucirkova argues that the rhythm of children's media shapes opportunities to reflect, understand a story and connect emotionally: constantly shifting cues may capture attention while leaving too little space to process.

item.title: AI support should follow demonstrated learning readiness, rather than replace foundational thinking from the outset.
item.description: Conceptual framework: AI support should follow demonstrated learning readiness, rather than replace foundational thinking from the outset. A proposed staged approach to AI use in formal learning; distinguish foundational independent work from guided and selective offloading.
